title: Optimizing Database Performance with Covert Index Scanning
explanation: Covert index scanning is an advanced database optimization technique where query planners bypass standard table heaps by satisfying read requests exclusively from secondary index structures containing redundant columns. This matters because it eliminates costly random I/O operations and row-lookup overhead during high-frequency read workloads. It works by projecting frequently queried payload attributes directly into the leaf nodes of a B-Tree index, transforming standard indexes into covering indexes that serve data in place. A practical use case is in high-throughput financial ledger systems, where account balance checks execute instantly without touching the primary storage table.
takeaway: Design database indexes to include frequently accessed projected columns, bypassing table heaps to drastically reduce disk I/O and accelerate high-concurrency read operations.
